This looks like a common scam
The message has something that looks like a Pix key. Before you pay, check with the person another way, like a phone call.
Scammers often ask for a fee by link to release a delivery. Do not pay through the link. Check the tracking in the store\'s app or on the Correios site.
This link\'s address copies a bank, a government office or a well-known company, but it is not the real one. Do not open the link. Use the app or the site you already use.
Banks do not send links to unblock an account, a card or Pix. Do not open the link. Open your bank\'s app and check there.
The message has a Pix copy-and-paste code. Before you pay, check with the person another way and look at the name your bank shows.
The message has a boleto code. Fake boletos are a common scam. Before you pay, check in your bank app who gets the money.
The message mentions a payment receipt. A screenshot of a receipt does not prove payment. Check in your bank app that the money arrived.
Scammers often pretend to be family and say they have a new number or account. Call the number you already have for the person and check that it is them.
Rush and money requests show up a lot in scams. Before you do anything, check with the person another way.
